tagline: A World Heritage city — old stupas scattered across open fields
introHtml: Sukhothai was one of Thailand's earliest capitals, and most people come to walk the historical park, full of ancient stupas and Buddha images sitting out in wide-open fields. You can cycle around the old town all day — the air is clear, the mood is quiet, and it never gets as crowded as the bigger tourist towns. If you have extra time, swing by Si Satchanalai nearby for a different set of ruins under bigger, shadier trees. Grab a bowl of the famous Sukhothai noodles, and take this town slowly.
bestTime: November–February, cool weather that's easy for walking and cycling around the ruins

highlights.name: Sukhothai Historical Park
highlights.blurb: A World Heritage old town with ancient stupas and Buddha images spread across open fields — easy to spend a whole day cycling through.

highlights.name: Wat Mahathat
highlights.blurb: The big temple at the heart of the old town, with its lotus-bud stupa and rows of Buddha images to walk among.

highlights.name: Wat Si Chum
highlights.blurb: A giant seated Buddha (Phra Achana) squeezed inside a narrow mondop — the photo stop everyone in Sukhothai makes.

highlights.name: Si Satchanalai Historical Park
highlights.blurb: Another ancient town, shadier and quieter, with fewer people — good for wandering the old stupas in peace.

highlights.name: Sukhothai noodles
highlights.blurb: The dish the town is known for, with long beans, peanuts, and stewed pork in a sweet-leaning broth — easy to find all over town.

highlights.name: Loy Krathong & Candle Festival
highlights.blurb: The big yearly event in the old town, with lanterns and a light show among the ruins — a really beautiful atmosphere.

foodScene.name: Sukhothai noodles
foodScene.note: The town's signature dish — thin rice noodles in a sweet-leaning broth with sliced long beans, peanuts, and pork. Several well-known shops.

foodScene.name: Khao poep
foodScene.note: A local stuffed steamed-rice-sheet dish eaten with hot soup — find it around Sawankhalok and in the markets.

foodScene.name: Northern Thai food
foodScene.note: Khao soi, nam ngiao, sai ua — found at shops around town, a northern style with a central-Thai touch.

foodScene.name: Morning market & street food
foodScene.note: The in-town markets have rice-and-curry plates, local sweets, and cheap breakfast bites to graze on.

foodScene.name: Cafes around the old town
foodScene.note: Small cafes have opened near the old town and in the city center — a nice spot to sit with a coffee after walking the ruins.

foodScene.name: Moo kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals — Thai-style grill-and-hotpot. Plenty of places to choose from at friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Sangkhalok ware & local sweets
foodScene.note: Besides the food, there's Sangkhalok pottery and local sweets to take home — easy to find at the souvenir shops.

attractions.name: Sukhothai Historical Park
attractions.blurb: A World Heritage old town — ancient stupas and Buddha images across wide fields, great to cycle or walk for a full day.

attractions.name: Wat Mahathat
attractions.blurb: The big temple at the center of the old town, with its lotus-bud stupa and rows of Buddha images, a top photo spot.

attractions.name: Wat Si Chum
attractions.blurb: The huge seated Phra Achana enshrined in a narrow mondop — you glimpse the face clearly through the door gap, an iconic shot.

attractions.name: Wat Sa Si
attractions.blurb: A Ceylonese-style stupa sitting in the middle of a pond in the old town, with lovely reflections especially at dawn and dusk.

attractions.name: Si Satchanalai Historical Park
attractions.blurb: An ancient town by the Yom River, shaded by big trees — quiet walks among old stupas and temples, never too busy.

attractions.name: Ramkhamhaeng National Park (Khao Luang)
attractions.blurb: A tall mountain with a trail up to the Khao Luang summit, with a sea of mist and varied plant life — good for hikers.

attractions.name: Sangkhalok kilns, Si Satchanalai
attractions.blurb: The site of the old Sangkhalok pottery kilns — learn about the ceramics that were once exported far and wide.

attractions.name: New Sukhothai town
attractions.blurb: The newer district along the Yom River, with restaurants, markets, and places to stay — a relaxed spot after the old town.

itineraryIdeas: Sukhothai for nature lovers — Khao Luang & Ramkhamhaeng
